claims.text: The target material is equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi.
Equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi exhibits significant chemical disorder.
Equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi exhibits intrinsic local lattice distortions.
Random chemical disorder produces local atomic-scale lattice distortions in the HEA.
Random chemical disorder induces local strain.
Disorder-induced local strain alters phonon dispersion.
Incorporating atomistic lattice-distortion effects into a predictive model improves its correlation with experimental thermal conductivity.
Combining distortion-aware DFT phonon calculations with machine-learning regression will improve thermal-conductivity predictions for equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi.
Conventional methods that omit detailed lattice distortions typically have thermal-conductivity prediction errors exceeding 30–40% for HEAs.
The hybrid framework will reduce prediction error to below 15%.
Predictions from the hybrid framework should remain within ±15% of measured thermal conductivity from 300 K to 800 K.
The approach is applicable when intrinsic lattice distortions caused by chemical disorder dominate phonon scattering.
The approach may be unreliable when grain boundaries or surface effects dominate thermal conductivity.
Laser-flash analysis will measure the alloy's thermal conductivity from 300 K to 800 K for validation.
A consistent prediction-to-measurement discrepancy greater than 20% would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to predict the thermal-conductivity trend over 300–800 K would falsify the hypothesis.
Accurately representing disorder in highly complex alloys may be computationally infeasible.
The available training data may be inadequate for the machine-learning model.
